title: Cohort convergence and reversion tactics (working draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft capturing pragmatic heuristics and operational steps for: cohort convergence (how canaries and A/B cohorts reach stable signal alignment), safe reversion strategies when signals diverge, and tactical decision flows for small-batch LLM rollouts. Focus is on cross-functional playbook language so PMs, SREs, ML engineers, and CS can act from the same mental model.

Scope and intent:
- Applies to user-visible LLM feature rollouts (hosted API, Dedicated, Private) where model variant or routing changes are introduced incrementally.
- Intended for medium-risk launches (non-PII processing, customer-facing behavior change). High-risk regulated rollouts should use the private-deployments safety matrix (see linked artifacts).
- Not prescriptive on statistical test choice; emphasizes operational thresholds and choreography.

Key definitions (working):
- Convergence: cohort metrics (latency, cost, quality evals, negative-signal rate) settling within a predefined tolerance band of control within a monitoring window.
- Divergence: any sustained breach of tolerance band for > T minutes or across > N independent signals.
- Soft Reversion: automated or manual traffic steering to a fallback variant at slice level (e.g., per region or organization) while retaining experiment artifacts and telemetry for root cause.
- Hard Reversion: full rollback of the feature across all slices and disabling of the experiment.

Signal taxonomy (primary / secondary / guardrails):
- Primary (must check for convergence):
  - Quality regressions from prompt set evals (regression rate vs baseline)
  - User-visible error spikes / failure rates (model-side errors, HTTP 5xx)
  - Latency p95 and p99 for affected routes
- Secondary (contextual):
  - Cost delta per 1k tokens (unit economics drift)
  - Engagement proxies (CTR for suggestion features, retention delta)
  - Human review queue backlog for HIL flows
- Guardrails (safety triggers):
  - Toxicity/NLP safety signals above threshold
  - Data exfiltration or PII detection alerts

Convergence heuristics (recommended):
1) Rolling window: 30m window with 10m evaluation cadence for early waves; expand to 3h window for broader cohorts.
2) Tolerance bands (example defaults, tune per product):
   - Quality regression: < 1.5% absolute regression vs baseline on core prompt set and < 3% on supplemental prompts
   - Latency p95: within +20% of baseline or absolute cap of 800ms (whichever is lower)
   - Error rate: delta < 0.05% absolute
   - Cost: expected delta within forecast band (projected spend variance < 10%)
3) Multi-signal confirmation: trigger divergence only when 2 independent primary signals breach tolerance or 1 primary + 1 guardrail.

Cohort convergence sequence (operator checklist):
- Pre-activation (day 0): smoke test on synthetic traffic; confirm observability hooks and trace ids; QA run documented in PR.
- Wave 1 (1% traffic / internal cohort): 15-30m warmup, monitor 30m windows, human-in-the-loop watch.
- Wave 2 (5% external): extend to 1h windows, confirm no quality regressions and cost estimates match.
- Wave 3 (20%): enable wider telemetry retention (capture example hits), start eval sweeps across prompt buckets.
- Full (100%): final safety sweep; if any primary signal breached during Waves 1-3, pause progression and run remediation steps.

Decision flow when divergence observed (runbook):
1) Triage (0-10m): on-call steward inspects dashboards (console route view, eval regressions, SLOs). If guardrail triggered -> immediate notification to safety & SRE.
2) Containment (10-30m): apply soft reversion to affected slices (geography/org/cohort). Document action in experiment log and mark hypothesis as "quarantined".
3) Investigation (30m-3h): gather trace examples, top N failing prompts, and compare model variant outputs vs control. Open a JIRA ticket with initial triage artifacts.
4) Remediation or rollback (3h-24h): if root cause fix available (prompt tweak, config change), test in canary and re-run waves. If no quick fix and user harm or strong regression, perform hard reversion.

Soft reversion tactics (practical patterns):
- Slice-level fallback: route only the affected slice to the previous stable variant (config in routing policy).
- Rate-limited throttling: reduce exposure by 50% and observe signal slope for 1-2 windows.
- Feature gating degrade: turn off downstream features that amplify the regression (e.g., remove reranking stage).

Hard reversion criteria (examples):
- Any guardrail violation (safety/policy) regardless of other signals.
- Quality regression >5% absolute on core prompt set persisting across two evaluation windows after containment.
- Rising error rate + latency spike suggestive of systemic overload or memory leak.

Observability & artifacts to collect for postmortem:
- Top 50 example prompts where variant differs most from control with timestamps.
- Full trace dumps for 1% sample of failed requests.
- Token-level cost breakdown for affected period.
- Eval sweep outputs and diff visualization.
- Slack thread history and action timeline (who flipped what config and when).

Cross-functional responsibilities (who does what):
- Product / PM: validate user-impact hypothesis, define acceptable tolerance bands for quality and engagement, communicate to stakeholders.
- ML/Applied: run targeted evals, propose prompt/kernel/latency mitigations, prepare model fallback builds.
- SRE/Platform: enact routing/fallback, monitor infra metrics, confirm autoscaling responses.
- Customer Success: surface impacted customer reports and prioritize customer-facing remediation comms.

Open questions / risks (to resolve before a broad rollout):
- How to weight combined signals when cost delta is favorable but quality regresses slightly? (tradeoff policy)
- Automated rollback vs manual sign-off threshold for Dedicated customers with custom routing rules.
- Retention of example hits for privacy-sensitive customers: need a policy knob to anonymize.

Quick templates (copy for activation note or incident):
- Activation note (short): wave=X, variant=alpha-v2, cohort=EU-prod, start=2025-02-19T10:12Z, steward=@aisha, telemetry-checks=[eval-reg, p95-lat, 5xx], baseline-link=<confluence>.
- Incident stub: time, observed-signal(s), action taken (soft/hard revert), tickets opened, owner for remediation.

Next steps (action items):
- (Aisha) finalize tolerance defaults for suggestion and composer features by 2025-02-28.
- (Priya) add privacy-preserving example capture to the telemetry backlog (JIRA-RLW-1534).
- (Tomás) prototype a slice-throttling automation that reduces exposure based on rolling regression slope.
- (Evan) create a lightweight dashboard template for cross-team "quick read" during waves.

Notes / ephemeral ideas:
- Consider an experimental "confidence leash": if model's internal uncertainty (logit / calibrator signal) falls below a threshold across top-K tokens, degrade to conservative variant. Might help avoid some semantic regressions.
- HIL (human-in-loop) fast path: enable short-lived reviewers to approve samples in Wave 2 for high-sensitivity features.

References and related docs:
- See rollout-conductor and staged-release stickers in console (internal).
- Related: synthetic-cohort-canary-recipes-and-run-notes (for simulation patterns).

If you're reviewing this: add concrete numbers for your product's baseline and annotate questions inline. This page should be the single source for the "how we converge and when we revert" choreography.

-- end working draft --
